why: `A.reset()` on a capitalised parameter, with two unrelated classes defining `reset`, is taken for an object of the class it is named after, a marked guess (step 9; the case dispatch/receiver-named-after-class); while a class has a property `reset`, the call may be a property's read and no class is guessed (matlab-lookup.ts, variableMethod). When `C.m`'s method `reset` turns into a property of the same name and back, `C.m` keeps every name it defines and only the kind of its `reset` changes, while the edge that must go ends in `A.m`, which the sync leaves alone: each step must end where a fresh index ends (project rule; step 13).

edit.C.m:
classdef C
    properties
        reset = 1;
    end
end

classdef C
    methods
        function r = reset(obj)
            r = 1;
        end
    end
end
